beneficiaryEvidence: Awesome Phone Call Agents is an early community hub for developers and workflow builders creating reusable phone-call workflows for AI agents. CALL-E SDKs, provider APIs, authentication, call execution, and provider-side controls belong upstream with CALL-E itself. This repository focuses on the community artifacts around those primitives: Agent Skills, workflow plugins, user-facing apps, examples, templates, and safety patterns.

beneficiaryEvidence: A personal assistant that brings your context together, helps you follow through, and prepares actions for review.

LIA is an open-source personal AI assistant in a web application you can host yourself. It connects the information you make available — emails, calendar, documents, preferences and commitments — to help you prepare conversations, organize your day and follow through.
taskEvidence: Smart multi-agent conversational assistant with LangGraph orchestration, Human-in-the-Loop, enterprise-grade observability, and full i18n support (6 languages)
A personal assistant that brings your context together, helps you follow through, and prepares actions for review.
outcomeEvidence: LIA also helps between conversations: a daily briefing, a personal **Radio**, reminders, routines and proactive suggestions. You choose the sources and enabled features, and the time windows and channels for proactive help. Chat, rich cards, voice and Live sessions keep this assistance accessible in the same application.

- A data card shows everything the source supplied and never invents a missing value — an e-mail's body, every organisation of a contact, conference join points, subtasks, a place's photos (full-screen gallery), reviews and opening hours, a route's alternatives, weather slots, generated-document previews — the detail behind native disclosures; opening one calls nothing. The model reads a versioned semantic view of the answer, never the card's HTML ([ADR-332](docs/architecture/ADR-332-Deterministic-Cards-Received-Facts-And-Message-Owned-Actions.md), [HTML_CARDS](docs/technical/HTML_CARDS.md)).

outcomeEvidence: MCP stdio programs require separate startup trust. agentLoop: 新工单进入 → 提取主题与风险信号 → 分类、去重、补全上下文 → 分派或生成草稿 → 人工发送与抽检。
successMetric: 缩短首次响应时间，提升一次解决率并降低错误升级率。
guardrail: 涉及退款、隐私、法律或安全事件时必须升级人工；Agent 不直接承诺补偿。

title: 安全告警证据归并与初步调查
frequency: 持续监控
summary: 把分散的告警、日志和资产信息归并为可审阅的调查包，帮助分析师优先处理高风险事件。
agentLoop: 告警触发 → 拉取允许范围内的上下文 → 关联相似事件与资产 → 生成证据时间线 → 安全分析师裁决。
successMetric: 缩短平均分诊时间，提高有效告警占比与调查证据完整度。
guardrail: 仅只读访问获授权的数据源；不得自行隔离资产、封禁账号或删除证据。

title: 文档转结构化业务流程
frequency: 每次政策、合同或流程更新
summary: 从规范、合同或操作手册中提取字段、步骤、例外和待确认项，生成可审阅的结构化工作项。
agentLoop: 上传或更新文档 → 提取关键字段和规则 → 标出不确定项与引用位置 → 人工确认 → 写入目标系统。
successMetric: 降低录入耗时与遗漏率，衡量字段准确率和人工修改率。
guardrail: 保留来源页码与引用；合同解释、法律结论和最终写入必须由授权人员确认。

title: 销售账户研究与会前准备
frequency: 每次重点会面
summary: 从获授权的 CRM、公开资料和历史互动中整理账户背景、机会、风险和建议问题。
agentLoop: 会议创建 → 汇总允许的数据源 → 生成带来源的简报与提问建议 → 销售确认 → 用于会前准备。
successMetric: 提高准备覆盖率、跟进及时率和有效会议转化率。
guardrail: 不得从非授权来源抓取个人数据；简报不得替代 CRM 中的人工事实核验。

title: 数据质量异常定位与修复提案
frequency: 每次数据管道运行
summary: 发现异常、追溯上游变更、估计影响范围，并生成可复现的修复建议。
agentLoop: 质量规则失败 → 对比历史与上游变更 → 生成异常说明、影响范围和修复 SQL 草案 → 数据负责人审核执行。
successMetric: 缩短异常恢复时间，降低重复故障与错误数据影响范围。
guardrail: Agent 只能读取生产数据并在隔离环境生成建议；写操作必须由数据负责人批准。

title: 浏览器后台操作与异常交接
frequency: 高频、规则明确
summary: 在权限受控的后台系统中完成查找、录入和状态更新，并在异常或高风险动作前暂停。
agentLoop: 合格请求触发 → 导航至已授权系统 → 读取与填写字段 → 校验结果 → 低风险操作执行，高风险操作请求确认。
successMetric: 减少单笔处理时长，追踪成功率、人工接管率和返工率。
guardrail: 支付、删除、对外发送和权限变更必须二次确认；每一步保留审计日志。

title: 会议纪要到行动项闭环
frequency: 每次关键会议
summary: 将会议记录整理为决策、负责人、截止时间、依赖关系和待澄清事项。
agentLoop: 会议结束 → 提取行动项与引用片段 → 指派建议负责人 → 参会者确认 → 同步至项目管理系统。
successMetric: 提升行动项确认率、按时完成率与会后跟进速度。
guardrail: 参会者确认前不应把推断的承诺或负责人写入正式系统。

In classical robotics, engineers decompose tasks, specify objectives, write control code, and repair failures before deployment. In *agentic robotics*, a foundation model (FM), usually a large language model (LLM) or vision-language model (VLM), makes some of these decisions at run time or while the system improves. This repository lists the systems analyzed in the survey and organizes them with the survey's taxonomy: where the FM takes part in generating behavior, which improvement decisions it makes, and how feedback is retained.

Agents with their own @handle, memory, skills, and per-channel permissions. 37 connector presets (Zendesk, Stripe, GitHub, HubSpot), MCP and API connections, scheduled work, coding sandbox. Manage from Slack, Admin, or MCP. Built on Flue. Cloudflare Workers or Node. Apache 2.0.

Chickpea gives your team AI teammates in Slack. You address them by name. `@support` answers the billing question in the channel where someone asked it. `@revops` posts Monday's pipeline numbers from HubSpot on a schedule. `@oncall` reads the repo before it answers. Each one has its own instructions, memory, connected accounts, and list of channels it's allowed to work in. You set all of that up by asking, in Slack.
outcomeEvidence: Every run rechecks the whole chain: is the Agent alive, does it still have the channel, is the creator still a member, do the required connections still work, does policy still allow it. If authority disappears, future runs pause. Chickpea never silently reassigns work to someone else. Cloudflare supplies alarms; the production Node launcher checks for due work at startup and every minute while its process is running.

Install the coding sandbox when an Agent needs a real checkout, package installation, tests, or a dev server. Open **Settings → Coding sandbox**, request installation, redeploy. It requires **Workers Paid**. The container application and its Ubuntu-based image live in your Cloudflare account and may incur costs on it, and the first image build takes several minutes. Node installations always use the standard in-memory bash sandbox and never touch the host filesystem or host git and SSH. Full procedure in the [coding sandbox runbook](docs/runbooks/coding-sandbox-deployment.md).
sceneEvidence: 4. **The reply lands in the thread under `@support`'s name and avatar,** streamed as it's written. The thread now belongs to `@support`. Publishing to a public channel joins the bot automatically. Private channels need someone to `/invite @Chickpea` first, and the grant stays pending until then. Where an Agent is published also decides who can DM it. In a public channel, any workspace member can. Only in private channels, only those members can. Unpublished, only its creator can.
